If you haven't made it to the Labor Day Lift Off yet — today is your last chance.

Colorado Springs' 50th annual balloon festival wraps up today at Prospect Lake in Memorial Park. Here's what's on tap for the final day:

🎈 Morning mass ascension: The balloons launch early, weather permitting. If you want to see 60 hot air balloons in the sky, get there early — this is the most spectacular part of the festival.

🎈 Evening Balloon Glow: Tonight's Balloon Glow is the signature closing event, where the balloons light up in the dark from their burners without leaving the ground. It's a magical experience for kids. Check current weather and schedule updates at the festival's official site.

It's free. It's at Memorial Park. And it's Labor Day — families are off school and work, the weather in September in Colorado Springs is typically beautiful, and this is genuinely one of the best free things to do in COS all year.

D11, D20, and D49 families: school's back tomorrow. Make today count.

Mark your calendars for this Saturday — Fiestas Patrias is coming to Colorado Springs.

The annual Fiestas Patrias Colorado festival is a free community celebration of Hispanic heritage and culture, happening September 12 in Colorado Springs (Pioneers Museum area and downtown). It's one of the most vibrant family events of the fall season, with something for everyone:

🎉 Live music and dancing
🤼 Lucha libre (Mexican wrestling) — a crowd favorite for kids
🍽 Food vendors with incredible variety
🎪 Cultural booths and activities

The festival celebrates the national independence days of Mexico, Chile, and other Latin American countries — which fall in mid-September — making it a great opportunity for families to experience the culture and history that is a significant part of Colorado Springs' community identity.

It's free to attend and family-friendly. Save Saturday, September 12 on your calendar.

stories.title: New Study — GLP-1 Weight Loss Drug Prescriptions for Kids Surged 65% After AAP Guidelines (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Prescriptions for weight-loss drugs like Wegovy for kids jumped 65% after the AAP's 2023 guidelines. Sevenfold increase from 2022-2024. What COS parents need to know before the next well-child visit. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 3:00 PM MT
Tier: 2

Have you heard about weight-loss medications being prescribed for kids? Here's what the research actually says.

When the American Academy of Pediatrics issued new guidelines in 2023 recommending medication alongside lifestyle changes for children with obesity, it triggered a significant shift in prescribing. According to studies published in 2025 and 2026:

📊 GLP-1 drug prescriptions for kids and teens jumped 65% immediately after the guidelines were released, then continued to grow another 5% per month.
📊 Between October 2022 and September 2024, total pediatric prescriptions increased sevenfold — from about 3,400 to over 24,000 per year.
📊 The drugs in question are the same ones making headlines in adults: semaglutide (Wegovy/Ozempic) and liraglutide (Saxenda).

The research shows these drugs do improve blood sugar control and weight in obese children. But gastrointestinal side effects — nausea, vomiting, diarrhea — are significantly more common than with placebo.

The good news: fewer than 10% of eligible kids are actually being prescribed these medications. This isn't widespread prescribing — it's a targeted tool for children with clinically diagnosed obesity.

If your pediatrician brings this up at your next well-child visit, it's worth an honest conversation about whether it's appropriate for your child's situation. You're not obligated to say yes — and you're also not out of line for asking questions.

stories.title: 1 in 5 Teens Are Asking AI Chatbots for Mental Health Advice (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: 1 in 5 teens has asked an AI chatbot for mental health advice, per an AAP survey. Back-to-school anxiety is real — here's how to create space for the conversation before they turn to a chatbot. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 5:00 PM MT
Tier: 2

Your teen might be talking to a chatbot about their mental health. According to an AAP survey, 1 in 5 adolescents and young adults has asked an AI chatbot — like ChatGPT — for mental health advice.

That's not inherently bad news. Teens seeking information and support is a healthy impulse. But AI chatbots aren't therapists, and they can't replace the kind of connection and context a real person provides. For a teen dealing with social anxiety, depression, or stress about school — the stakes of bad advice are real.

Back-to-school season is when teen anxiety tends to spike. New classes, social dynamics shifting, academic pressure ramping up — it's a lot. And many teens won't initiate the conversation with a parent or counselor. If AI is filling that gap, it's worth knowing.

A few things parents can do:

✅ Ask open-ended questions at the end of school days ("What was the hardest part today?" not "How was school?")
✅ Normalize mental health conversations by talking about your own stress sometimes
✅ Know your district's counseling resources — D11, D20, and D49 all have school counselors; make sure your kid knows theirs by name
✅ If your teen won't talk to you, that's normal — but make sure they have *someone*: a coach, an aunt/uncle, a trusted adult

Has your family talked about what to do when things feel overwhelming?

stories.title: Labor Day Routines Reboot — How to Reset After a Long Weekend (TIER 3)

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: D49 families: week 6 starts tomorrow. D11: week 4. D20: week 3. Labor Day is the natural reset point. Quick tips for getting bedtimes back on track tonight. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 10:00 AM MT
Tier: 3

Happy Labor Day, COS parents. Tomorrow, school is back in session — and a three-day weekend has a way of sliding bedtimes, meal schedules, and morning routines sideways.

Here's where things stand for local families: D49 starts week 6 on Tuesday, D11 starts week 4, and D20 starts week 3. The honeymoon phase of the new school year is well behind us at this point. What you set up tonight matters for how Tuesday morning goes.

A few simple resets for tonight:

🌙 Bedtime: The AASM recommends 9-12 hours of sleep for ages 6-12 and 8-10 hours for teens. If the long weekend pushed bedtime back an hour or two, aim to close half that gap tonight. Don't try to force the full correction at once — gradual works better than sudden.

🍽 Prep tonight: Pack backpacks, sign permission slips, lay out tomorrow's clothes, prep anything you can for lunch. Tuesday morning chaos is mostly a Sunday night problem.

📱 Screens off earlier: If screens were allowed later over the weekend, start pulling them back tonight. Blue light disrupts melatonin, and tired kids (and parents) don't do their best work on Tuesdays.

You've got this. Summer's over. Routine is actually good for kids — they just don't always know it yet.
